---
title: "Wade In"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will choose how much of your data and your machine to hand over for one task, and start at the lowest step that gets the job done.
- **Before you start:** [Know Your Gear](know-your-gear.html), and Python 3 for the exercise. Your own data agreement overrides anything here.
- **Time:** about 20 minutes.
:::

## The scene

A manager needs a status report across projects, kept in a spreadsheet. A data analyst needs a count of samples received per project from the project database, using SQL (the language for querying a database). Both have two worries: where the data goes, and the belief that using an LLM means letting an agent loose on their computer.

Between "never" and "the agent runs my machine" there are several steps, and many useful tasks sit on the lower ones. You may stop at any step.

## Two dials

1. **What leaves your machine?** With a hosted model, anything you type, paste or upload is sent to the provider, and so is anything an agent reads. A local model keeps prompts on your machine, though web or tool calls it makes may still reach out.
2. **What may the tool do?** Produce text, read files, edit files, or run commands.

Each dial needs its own decision. A chat window has a low second dial and can still send a whole pasted table. A read-only agent (it can read files but not change them) sends whatever it reads.

## The ladder

| Step | Manager (spreadsheet) | Analyst (database) | What leaves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Build the table by hand | Write the query yourself | nothing |
| 1 | Ask for an outline, no data | Ask how to explain a fall in samples | your words |
| 2 | Headings and invented rows; you apply the formula | Schema only; you run the query read-only | names and invented rows |
| 3 | Small allowed extract, or a local model | Small allowed extract or local model, for free-text notes | the extract; nothing if local |
| 4 | Read-only agent on a copy | Read-only agent on a copy | everything it reads |
| 5 | Agent edits and runs commands | Agent edits and runs pipeline code | everything it reads, plus whatever its commands send |

Pasting the results of a step 2 task back into the chat sends those rows too, which makes it step 3. Plan mode (the agent reads and proposes, and does not edit) belongs to step 4: a copy protects the original from edits, and anything the agent reads is still sent.

## Three questions before any step

1. **What kind of data is it?** The table gives a typical starting point. Your agreement and your data steward decide, and they can be stricter. A data steward is the person at your organisation who looks after data rules.
2. **Which account will you use?** Consumer and organisation accounts have different terms (next section).
3. **What leaves at this step?** Say it in one sentence before you press enter.

| Kind of data | Typical starting point |
|---|---|
| Public or published | Any step |
| Internal, not personal | Steps 1 to 3; 4 to 5 on an approved account, on a copy |
| Personal, including pseudonymised codes (codes that replace names) | Steps 0 to 2, invented rows only |
| Health, genetic or otherwise controlled | Steps 0 to 2, unless your agreement says otherwise in writing |

Pseudonymised codes still count as personal data. Small counts can single people out, so check your policy before pasting results for rare groups. Real or personal data is not pasted into consumer chat.

## What a chat window keeps

- **Training:** consumer accounts (Free, Pro, Max) have a setting that lets chats improve the models; with it on, data may be kept for up to 5 years. The setting is in your privacy settings.
- **Account type:** commercial accounts (such as Claude for Work and the API) are not used for training and delete inputs and outputs within 30 days by default. Check the plan in your account settings, or ask your administrator.
- **Deleted chats:** they leave the provider's storage within 30 days.
- **Incognito chats:** not used for training, and still kept for 30 days by default.
- **Screenshots, images and uploads:** treat them as data you share, like pasted text.
- **Other providers:** their chat tools have their own terms. Read them.

## Hands-on (data analyst): count samples without handing over the data

Save [make_db.py](../../exercises/basecamp/wade-in/make_db.py), [run_query.py](../../exercises/basecamp/wade-in/run_query.py), [report-query.sql](../../exercises/basecamp/wade-in/report-query.sql) and [check-samples.sql](../../exercises/basecamp/wade-in/check-samples.sql) into an empty folder. Every row is invented, and no LLM is called.

1. Run `python3 make_db.py` (or `python`). It writes `mock.db` and `schema-only.txt`. The text file holds table and column names and no rows, which is all that goes into a chat at step 2. This table-and-column outline is the **schema**. Names such as `participant_code` and `notes` hint at the real data, so decide whether even the names are fine to send.
2. Write the prompt you would send: paste the schema and ask for one read-only query giving, per project, the samples received and the open milestones (`done = 0`). Say you will run it yourself and do not want to paste rows.
3. `report-query.sql` stands in for the reply. Check it is a single `SELECT` (a query that only reads) on the tables you expect, then run `python3 run_query.py report-query.sql`. The script opens the database read-only, so a `DELETE` fails.
4. Run `python3 run_query.py check-samples.sql`, a count the model did not write, and compare:

   | Project | Model: samples | Your check: samples | Model: open milestones | Actual open milestones |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | Heron | 22 | 11 | 22 | 2 |
   | Kelp | 28 | 14 | 28 | 2 |
   | Vega | 34 | 17 | 34 | 2 |

5. The query ran without an error and its numbers are wrong. Each project has two open milestones, and the join (how two tables are matched row by row) pairs every sample with every open milestone, so each sample is counted twice. Fix the query, then run both again until Heron shows 11 and 2.

Only the schema and the query text left your machine. Running without an error and being right are separate questions, so check against a second query.

## Hands-on (manager): the same check in a spreadsheet

At step 2, paste only the column headings (Project, Milestone, Owner, Status) and two or three invented rows, and ask for a formula that counts open milestones per project. Apply it to your real sheet yourself. Check it with `COUNTIF` on one project's rows. If each of three projects has 6 rows and the formula shows 18 for every project, it counted the whole column. Find out why before the number goes in the report.

## Climbing, if and when you want to

- Move up a step when the lower step cannot do the task and you can say what leaves.
- Before steps 4 and 5, work on a copy, keep a way to undo, and limit what the agent may do.
- For sensitive data, stay on a local model when your agreement allows that copy.
- If you pasted something you should not have, stop and tell your data steward.
- Ask your steward: "I want to use [tool, account type] at step [n]. What leaves is [what]. Is that allowed for [data kind]?"

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Is my data used for model training? (consumer)](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023580-is-my-data-used-for-model-training): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it is the page that says the training setting exists for Free, Pro and Max chats, which decides your first account question.
- [How long do you store my data?](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it gives the 5-year and 30-day figures for consumer chats and what happens after you delete one.
- [How long do you store my organization's data?](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it is the commercial-account counterpart, with the 30-day default and the cases that keep data longer.
- [Use incognito chats](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12260368-use-incognito-chats): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it shows what incognito does and does not change, so you do not over-trust the name.
- [Data usage (Claude Code)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it states that the agent sends prompts and outputs over the network, which is what makes steps 4 and 5 different from running a query yourself.
- [Ollama FAQ](https://docs.ollama.com/faq): Ollama, docs. Why read: it says local runs do not send prompts to Ollama and separates its cloud models, which matters if you choose a local model for sensitive data.
- [AI for Science: the short version](https://aiforscience.eu/short-version/): AI for Science, article. Why read: a one-page European draft summary of research practices, useful for a conversation with your data steward. It is a draft without endorsements.
:::
